Study dashboard

A static page that reads nothing but the imported review log. Every figure is fixed at generation time; there is no script and no outbound request. It is also the importer's acceptance test — Mochi's own dashboard is a known-correct answer, so agreement means the import is right.

Read it this way: retention above 96% means the intervals are shorter than they need to be. The target set here is 90% — Zach's choice, not FSRS's default of 90% — and the collection sits +6.24 points above it. Paying for retention you already have, every day, is SPEC's objection, and "retention vs interval" below is what makes that payment visible.

On times of day: all 103,110 reviews carry time_unknown = 1. Mochi stored the date only and wrote midnight JST, so an hour-of-day analysis is impossible in principle. Rather than manufacture a false spike at 00:00, retention_by_hour is left empty.

activity · reviews per day

One cell is one day. Colour is the quartile of the review count, using thresholds shared across the whole span so one year is comparable with the next. A day with no study gets its own colour for zero — never the same colour as a day with one review. Dates are cut by each review's own tz_offset.

retention vs interval a tile Mochi lacks

The x axis is the preceding review interval. The boundaries are defined exactly once, in views.sql's review_log_bucketed; this page only names them. "Interval" has two definitions and this chart draws both: elapsed (reviews.elapsed_days — the gap that actually happened, filled) and scheduled (reviews.scheduled_days — the gap the scheduler intended, dashed and hollow). "unknown" is a review with no preceding interval under that definition. The line is the 90% target.

Reviews per bucket (elapsed / scheduled)

elapsed — the gap that happenedscheduled — the gap intendedhorizontal line = 90% target

Read it this way: on the elapsed basis the 90% target is missed in no bucket at all, worst at 60-180d, 93.34%. Every other band is ABOVE target, which means reviewing at shorter intervals than necessary. Even the longest observed band, > 365d, sits at 96.89% — and that is the evidence behind the claim that these intervals have room to grow.

Why the two definitions disagree completely at > 365d. Elapsed shows 3,217 reviews at 96.89% retention; scheduled shows 0. Scheduled is zero not because Mochi never planned beyond a year — it planned 1,386 of them, out to 2,707 days — but because scheduled_days means "the interval the PRECEDING review planned", so anything whose matching review has not happened yet cannot appear in the aggregate. 1,378 tracks are planned beyond a year, and their due dates run 2027-03-17 to 2033-10-17: not one has arrived. That is why this page reads elapsed as the observation. BACKTEST.md scores on the same basis, and the > 365d count agrees at 3,217 in both.

The 365-day cap was lifted on 2026-02-22. Before that, zero reviews were planned beyond a year; since, 1,386 have been, out to 2,707 days. Tracks sitting on exactly the cap (365 days) number 3,417 of 9,011 = 37.92%. Of those, 3,306 were last reviewed BEFORE the lift, so they are parked on a plan a post-lift Mochi would not have chosen — that is the constraint still actually in force. The longest interval that has actually elapsed, though, is 454 days, so beyond that everything is outside observation either way.

The overall 96.24% hides the variation. This charts decks that hold cards directly, with at least 300 reviews of their own, ordered by review count, with forward and reverse as separate points. Both the points and the selection use that deck's own reviews only; subtotals including child decks are in the table instead, so no row mixes two denominators. The thin line joining the pair is the gap between them.

forwardreversevertical line = 90% targethollow point = fewer than 100 reviews (small sample)

forecast

As of 2026-09-06. Over the 30 days that follow, 1,256 reviews are scheduled — 41.9 a day. The 526 already due on or before that date (489 of them from earlier still) are NOT in the bars: that is a backlog, not a forecast. The 3,907 unstudied cards are excluded too, because they carry no due date.

Where these bars come from. Of the 8,490 due in future, 8,490 carry a due date imported from Mochi and 0 carry one Hashigo issued. An imported track keeps Mochi's due date until it is graded here — deliberately. So this chart becomes Hashigo's one card at a time, with every grade.

acceptance test · 2026

Mochi's figures come from a screenshot of the user's own dashboard (notes/dashboard-reconciliation.md). Nothing here has been tuned to agree with them. Active days and retention matching exactly shows the window and the track selection are right. It is not an acceptance signal for the timezone, though — in this window there is no review on either 2026-01-01 or 2025-12-31, so cutting dates by JST or by UTC gives the same 14,420 reviews over 211 days for 2026 (measured). What actually pins JST is the all-time span: the first day 2022-06-28 and the last 2026-09-06 both shift by one under UTC.

The +1,176 review difference — Mochi reporting 8.2% fewer than this page — is not an import error: the import matches the export byte for byte at 103,110 reviews. notes/dashboard-reconciliation.md records eight candidate definitions tried and rejected. The leading one is "count one card once per day", which in this window gives 13,255 — +15 away from Mochi's 13,240. It leaves 0.11% unexplained, so it is left written down as a hypothesis, and the figure shown stays the grading-event count, whose definition is unambiguous.

What the words on this page mean

  • reviews — the number of grading events, counting every track — forward, reverse and cloze.
  • cards studied — distinct cards graded at least once inside the window.
  • active days — the number of days with at least one grading. Dates are cut by each review's own tz_offset, not by UTC.
  • days — both ends included. The window stops at the last review date.
  • retention — passed / all grading events.
  • study time — the sum of durations. A review carrying no duration contributes nothing.
  • preceding interval — how long it had been since that card was last seen. Mochi's interval is the next interval, so this is derived from the previous record at import time.

About this page

Generated by src/dashboard/render.ts. No script, no outbound request, no webfont — it opens from a file:// URL on a device with the radio off. Every aggregate chart has a matching table (by year, by month, by bucket, by deck). The activity heatmap's daily values are in the per-year tables too, all 1,333 of them — every day that carries a value can be read from a table. Days with no reviews have only the cell's title, and it holds no figure. Colours were chosen separately for light and dark and run through the data-viz validator.
